title: Tesla Cybercab In Texas Gets Stuck In Endless Loop, Leaving Passenger Trapped For 14 Minutes Until Support Intervenes
key_facts: Robotaxi rider David Moss says a Tesla Cybercab in Texas drove in loops around a pickup car park for seven minutes without finding an exit.
Tesla support then called, remotely stopped the car, and needed another seven minutes to restart the car's software (FSD) before he could finish the ride.
Moss posted the 14-minute episode on X; he says the car failed to reroute when it met road work.
He says a nearby construction crew moved a vehicle to make room but it did not help.
Moss said Tesla may have restarted FSD and altered the route; the article gives no Tesla response.
BroBible notes Cybercab service in Austin runs only until 11 p.m.
quote_evidence: A man recently found himself stuck inside a Tesla Cybercab for 14 minutes as the driverless vehicle repeatedly drove in circles, prompting intervention from Tesla support.
Moss posted the entire 14-minute episode on his X account, and the Tesla Cybercab was, as he said, just driving around in circles for seven of those minutes.
why_it_matters_hint: A driverless taxi that cannot reroute can leave riders waiting for remote staff to fix it.
notes: Single source: the rider's own post on X. His quoted post calls the car a 'Tesla Robotaxi'; BroBible calls it a Cybercab, so the vehicle type is not independently confirmed. He did finish his trip, so 'trapped' overstates. Austin is named only in the operating-hours remark.
